confidence: Kumon's observed rice in nominal monme, 1712-1718, nearly three times Kyoho's, in the "current silver" of Kusama's entries: the Hoei, Eiji, Mitsuho and Yotsuho silvers, dealt in as one with no rate of their own. Its grams are the 1714 law's (2 of current for 1 of Keicho); they cancel in a conversion. The ryo and mon rates are Kusama's (1815), and 1715-1716 are SILENT. The wage is borrowed.

monme.note: Current silver (1712-1718), 1.50 g pure by the 1714 law's 2 for 1 of Keicho; Kusama's market rates of 1712-1714 and 1717 (about 65-93 monme a ryo, 40-59 mon a monme), the mean of the rows' midpoints

bu.note: A quarter of a ryo (the gold count: 4 bu a ryo)

shu.note: A sixteenth of a ryo (16 shu a ryo)

rice.label: historical
rice.note: 0.840 monme a kg, Kumon's observed 1712-1718 (7 years)

wage.note: BORROWED: none found for these years; the reference day (0.907 monme) chained by Kumon's farm-servant year, 109.9 monme in 1712-1718 and 113.9 in 1745-1754, in grams of silver
